title: Node.js app hosting
description: Always-on Node.js containers with 512 MB of RAM and 1 CPU, built from your source with no Dockerfile.

title: Postgres database
description: One Postgres 16 database per project, with TLS, a public connection string and a shadow database for Prisma.

title: S3 storage
description: One S3 compatible bucket per project. Use any S3 client, with files public by URL.

title: Transactional email (coming soon)
description: Transactional email for your apps is coming soon. It is not available yet.

title: Scheduled API calls
description: Call any public HTTP or HTTPS URL on an interval from 1 minute to 30 days, with custom method, headers and body.

title: Custom domains
description: Point your domain at your app with a CNAME or A record, and EasyHost issues the certificate.

title: AI Builder
description: Describe an app in the dashboard and AI builds the frontend and the backend, live at <name>.easyhost.fun while you chat.

title: Team members
description: Invite people to a project by email. Members manage everything in it; only the owner can invite, remove, rename or delete.

title: ezhst CLI
description: Every EasyHost feature is available from one CLI with JSON output and no prompts in automation.

title: Agent skill
description: A single SKILL.md file that teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other agents to deploy and manage your app.

title: Pricing and limits
description: EasyHost hosting is free with no credit card. See every limit: 3 projects, 3 apps per project, Postgres, S3 storage and schedules.

title: Privacy policy
description: What EasyHost collects, why, who processes it, and why your data is not encrypted by us unless you encrypt it yourself.

title: Terms and conditions
description: The rules for using EasyHost: acceptable use, no encryption by default, our right to review and remove content, beta status and no warranty.

title: What is a platform as a service?
description: A platform as a service (PaaS) runs your application for you. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is object storage?
description: Object storage keeps files as objects in a flat bucket, each addressed by a key rather than a folder path. A short explanation for developers.

title: What does S3 compatible mean?
description: S3 compatible storage accepts the same API calls as Amazon S3, so existing SDKs and tools work after changing the endpoint and credentials.

title: What is a presigned URL?
description: A presigned URL is a temporary link that grants one specific S3 action, such as uploading a single file, without sharing your secret keys.

title: What is a database connection string?
description: A connection string is one URL holding everything a client needs to reach a database: username, password, host, port, database name and options such as sslmode.

title: What is database connection pooling?
description: A connection pool keeps a small set of open database connections and shares them between requests. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a Prisma shadow database?
description: A shadow database is a temporary database that prisma migrate dev uses to detect schema drift and check migrations. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a database migration?
description: A migration is a versioned change to your database schema, stored in your repository alongside your code. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is an environment variable?
description: An environment variable is a named value given to a process when it starts. A short explanation for developers.

title: Build-time vs runtime environment variables
description: Build-time variables are read while your app compiles, and their values get baked into the output. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a cron job?
description: A cron job is a task that runs automatically on a schedule, such as sending a daily report or cleaning old rows. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a CNAME record?
description: A CNAME record makes one hostname an alias of another, so www.example.com can follow my-app.easyhost.fun. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a DNS A record?
description: An A record maps a hostname directly to an IPv4 address. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is DNS propagation?
description: DNS propagation is the delay before a DNS change is seen everywhere. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a TLS certificate?
description: A TLS certificate proves that a server owns a domain and enables encrypted HTTPS connections. A short explanation for developers.

title: Serverless vs always-on containers
description: Serverless functions start per request and scale automatically, but can have cold starts, time limits and no long-lived connections.

title: What is a cold start?
description: A cold start is the delay when a platform must start your code before answering a request. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is server-side rendering?
description: Server-side rendering (SSR) builds HTML on the server for each request, then sends it to the browser. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a lockfile?
description: A lockfile records the exact version of every installed package, including nested ones. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is a monorepo?
description: A monorepo keeps several apps and packages in one repository, usually with one lockfile at the root. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is an agent skill?
description: An agent skill is a Markdown file of instructions that a coding agent loads when a task matches it. A short explanation for developers.

title: What is llms.txt?

title: What is an ephemeral filesystem?
